title: Proto exporter anchor manifest
description: Schema for analysis/handoff/contracts/proto/anchor_manifest.json produced by skills/proto-from-context/scripts/generate_proto.py (v1.3.2). Extends governance/schemas/sidecar_anchor_manifest.base.schema.json with proto-specific discriminators (sidecar literal `proto-from-context`, path extension `\.proto$`, view-element-kind enum {Service, Rpc, Message, Enum}, format discriminator `proto3`, structured unmapped_anchors array). The exporter is operator-driven (NOT a sidecar in the orchestrator-detection sense), but reuses the sidecar manifest base shape so downstream tooling that reads sidecar manifests can also read this exporter's manifest without special-casing. F5 does NOT validate this schema (the exporter writes operator-side artifacts under analysis/handoff/, not canonical state); the schema is consumed by tests/test_generate_proto.py and by future downstream consumers that want to verify exporter output before shipping. Mirrors v1.3.1 asyncapi-from-context schema with proto-shape adjustments (Service/Rpc instead of Channel/Operation, format const proto3 instead of asyncapi-3.0, duplicate_rpc_collision reason instead of duplicate_channel_collision, NEW proto_identifier_synthesis_failed reason for paths that pass shape but fail proto3 identifier synthesis).

format.description: Discriminator for spec-version drift. v1.3.2 emits proto3 only; proto2 is intentionally not supported (proto3 is the modern default for gRPC). Future spec extensions (proto3-edition, etc.) would extend the enum.

view_element_id.description: Proto element identifier. Service entries use the synthesized service name (single proto3 identifier, e.g., `Orders`); Rpc entries use `<Service>.<Method>` (two dot-joined proto3 identifiers, e.g., `Orders.Created`); Message entries (reserved for future) would use the message name (single identifier); Enum entries (reserved for future) would use the enum name (single identifier). v1.3.2 emits Service + Rpc only. Service entries are deduplicated across multiple rpcs sharing the same service block (one Service entry per distinct synthesized service). v1.3.2 R1 fix: pattern matches the actual emitted shape — `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)?$` — so the schema enforces the same proto3 identifier grammar that `_synthesize_service_method` produces and `services.proto` renders. Reach equality across (a) synthesis output, (b) proto3 grammar, (c) this schema constraint is now atomic.

view_element_kind.description: Proto element kind. v1.3.2 emits Service + Rpc only; Message + Enum are reserved for future structured-input releases.

notes.description: Optional free-text annotation. Common content: original ClaimID/A51Ref this anchor traces to (mirrored into the proto rpc's bsa-anchor comment); rationale for the rpc placeholder when the operator should refine; for Service entries deduplicated across multiple anchors, may note that the entry is shared.

anchor_status.description: v1.3.7+: machine-readable promotion status. 'candidate' = exporter produced a v1.3.0+ skeleton placeholder for this anchor (no real message field schemas synthesized — operator must enrich the .proto before shipping). 'promoted' is reserved for future releases that auto-synthesize real shapes from interface_contract_model.md. v1.3.0..v1.3.6 emitted no anchor_status (legacy consumers should treat absence as 'candidate'); v1.3.7+ emits 'candidate' explicitly so 'this is a skeleton, enrich it' is grep-able from CI / release-readiness gates.

unmapped_anchors.description: A61 anchors that were considered for inclusion but skipped, with structured reasons. Empty when every contract-class anchor produced a service+rpc pair. Operator-readable signal: 'X anchors couldn't be auto-materialized; review and decide'.

reason.description: Why the anchor was skipped. `non_contract_anchor_class` — AnchorClass != contract (the exporter materializes only contract-class anchors). `element_id_not_path_shaped` — ElementID doesn't match `^/[A-Za-z0-9_/{}.~-]*$` (ASCII-exact path characters; `%` is intentionally rejected — see exporter docstring), OR has malformed OpenAPI-style template syntax (unbalanced / empty / nested / misordered `{...}`), OR contains a `{...}` template whose name doesn't match the proto3 field-name grammar `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` (illegal template names like `{order-id}` (hyphen — legal in v1.3.1 AsyncAPI but illegal in proto3), `{9id}` (leading digit), `{tenant.id}` (dot), `{user id}` (space), `{order/sub}` (slash) rejected at the shape gate; v1.3.2 R1 lesson — the gate's template-name charset must equal the downstream proto3 field-name grammar, NOT a sibling exporter's permissive charset), OR is a dot-style address like `OrderService.CreateOrder` (v1.3.2 supports only path-style; dot-style deferred to v1.3.2.x). `element_id_path_traversal` — ElementID contains a literal `..` (encoded variants like `%2e%2e` are blocked by the path-shape gate above and surface as `element_id_not_path_shaped`). `duplicate_rpc_collision` — two anchors map to the same `<Service>.<Method>` rpc address; first wins, rest skipped. `proto_identifier_synthesis_failed` — ElementID passed all shape gates but the proto-identifier synthesis pass couldn't produce valid proto3 service+method names (e.g., all-template path `/{a}/{b}` has no segment for service name; first segment starts with digit `/123abc/foo` PascalCases to a non-identifier; root path `/` has no segments at all).

element_id.description: Optional: the original ElementID, surfaced for operator triage.
